stock.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on six-month return against spy, gross profit over assets, gross margin trend — revenue +11.5% over the trailing year, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

evidence.label: Earnings yield / free cash flow yield

stock.peerBasis: 8 candidates in SIC major group 51, compared on free cash flow yield, all from the same source and the same periods.

stock.counterargument: It is an expensive stock: 43.8× trailing earnings and a 4.0% free cash flow yield, so the growth is already in the price and one weak quarter would cost a lot. debt is 3.24× trailing operating cash flow, which leaves less room if conditions turn. growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +12.9%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $87.17 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-10-23, 10 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-03.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-11) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
stories.excerpt: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to create incentives for powerful AI models that make following the rules the most rational choice. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words…
stories.lead:
As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law, hack into unauthorized servers, or release poison gas into major cities and kill us all.

Until now, this work has mostly focused on trying to peer into an AI’s “brain” to understand what it is “thinking,” or training models to hew to values that we hold dear. Claude, for instance, has its constitution—a sort of moral code.

stories.title: Coming in 2027: Apple’s $1,000 home robot for FaceTime and switching on lights

stories.lead:
Apple’s new CEO, John Ternus, is apparently pushing the tech company’s development of household robots—and the first to debut may be a home robot designed to autonomously roam around while supporting FaceTime calls and switching lights on whenever a person enters the room.

People who worked on Apple’s robotic projects told The Information that the AI-driven home robot, code-named J595, could be named HomeView Ultra in line with Apple’s new HomeView stationary smart display. The company is reportedly aiming to launch the robotic product with a possible price tag of $1,000 or more by 2027, although development delays may push that back to 2028.

stories.title: Death toll hits 29 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with 48 still missing
stories.excerpt: Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, President Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.
stories.lead:
KYIV, Ukraine — The death toll from a Russian attack in southern Ukraine on a site where people had gathered to receive humanitarian aid rose to 29 on Tuesday, with 48 still missing, as a wave of overnight strikes targeted power plants across the country, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people.

Dozens of rescuers and volunteers continued to search the cratered blast site of a destroyed aid facility and shelter in Komyushuvakha, a village in Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia region, hoping to find missing residents alive under the rubble. Instead, more bodies were pulled out and carried away in white plastic sheeting.

stories.title: US strikes Iranian island ahead of midterm elections
stories.excerpt: US officials described the attacks on Qeshm Island as limited and defensive, according to CBS, the BBC's US partner.
stories.lead:
The US has carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, US officials have told CBS, the BBC's US partner.

The officials described the strikes as limited and defensive, and said they were in response to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) firing on a US aircraft.

Iranian state news agency Irna reported explosions on Qeshm on Monday. The IRGC did not comment but said its forces had shot down two US MQM-170 drones south of the island and a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
stories.excerpt: The move comes barely a week after Rwanda's defence ministry was hit with sanctions by the US Treasury.
stories.lead:
US President Donald Trump has notified Congress of his intention to remove South Africa and Rwanda from a preferential trade programme, from 1 January 2027.

The African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa) allows eligible African countries to export thousands of products to the US duty-free.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement that an annual review had found that both countries were engaging in practices inconsistent with the programme's eligibility requirements.

stories.title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why
stories.excerpt: Britons have become less engaged with the jobs they do and are less willing to put in extra effort, a report has found.
stories.lead:
The so-called "quiet quitting" trend where workers do the basic requirements of a job but refuse to do anything more might be hitting the economy, analysis has found.

Over the last decade, Britons have become less engaged with the jobs they do and are less willing to put in extra effort, according to a Resolution Foundation report.

The thinktank said this could partly help explain the slump in productivity since the pandemic.

stories.title: Every quarter counts: W4L launches in Croatia with a scoring system built for drama
stories.excerpt: A new amateur water polo league is in the water. The Amateur Water Polo League, branded W4L, opened its 2026 Croatian season in Zadar with ten […] The post Every quarter counts: W4L launches in Croatia with a scoring system built for drama appeared first on Total Waterpolo .
stories.lead: In W4L, the final score does not decide the result. Every quarter is played as its own contest: a quarter win is worth 2 league points, a drawn quarter gives 1 point to each team and a lost quarter gives nothing. With four quarters, there are 8 points on the table in every game, and the possible results are 8:0, 7:1, 6:2, 5:3 and 4:4.

stories.title: Harvard Dominates Crosstown Rival in the Pool
stories.excerpt: Men's water polo matches season-high scoring in 21-11 win over MIT.
stories.lead:
CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- The No. 19 Harvard men's water polo team matched its season-high in scoring in a 21-11 NWPC win over MIT at Blodgett Pool on Sunday afternoon. The win moved the Crimson over .500 at 13-12 overall and 6-1 in conference play.

The Engineers (7-15, 1-6) hung around for the first half and into the third quarter; trailing by three at the first two intermissions. Harvard completely overwhelmed MIT in the fourth quarter; stretching a 15-10 lead by outscoring the visitors 6-1 in the final frame. Harvard's 21 goals matched its season-high previously set at MIT last month.
